item.description:
Yingqi Jia, Chen Feng
Hong Kong's multilevel pedestrian networks require travellers to navigate connections between buildings and floors. This makes wayfinding more complex and difficult. Evidence remains limited on which places and spatial situations are associated with getting lost, and on how spatial conditions, navigation information and personal characteristics explain these difficulties. item.title: DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A ROLE-BASED WEB ASSESSMENT PLATFORM FOR NIGERIAN UNIVERSITIES USING THE LARAVEL MVC FRAMEWORK
item.description:
Innocent Adjaino, Omolegho A. Ibok
In many Nigerian universities, assessment still means printed scripts, long marking weekends and results that reach students weeks after the examination. This paper describes the design and implementation of a web-based student assessment system built to take that burden off lecturers while keeping the process fair and traceable. Estimating investor-specific demand curves, we find that Robinhood traders are fundamentally distinct from all other investors, including other households: their demand is the most elastic and tilts most strongly toward volatile and microcap stocks. Quadratic programs (QPs) are a core building block in many applications. In practice, constraints are often softened with slack variables to guarantee feasibility. The standard approach tackles this by introducing additional decision variables, growing the resulting optimization problem. High-fidelity digital twins in continuous biomanufacturing are often bottlenecked by incomplete kinetic models, while standard data-driven algorithms (e.g., SINDy, PINNs) lack interpretability or impose rigid physical assumptions. Shuqi Wang, Yunhai Xiao, Mengjiao Shi
This paper proposes a square-root clustered Lasso penalized method for high-dimensional linear regression. By integrating square-root loss with the clustered Lasso penalty, the resulting method enables flexible regression modeling and allows tuning parameter selection independent of the unknown noise level. We develop a unified framework for assortment optimization and matching under multinomial logit (MNL) choice, yielding simple algorithms and analyses across a broad class of problems. We consider decentralized stochastic nonconvex optimization over directed networks. Push--Pull provides an efficient decentralized optimization framework for such networks, but in the stochastic setting, gradient variance can slow its convergence and complicate the analysis of linear speedup. item.description:
Lukang Sun
We prove global well-posedness and regularization for the isotropic consensus-based optimization equation with initial probability measures of finite fourth moment. Under suitable weight decay assumptions, after any nonconstant consensus motion, both the density and the consensus trajectory become smooth, and all spatial Sobolev norms are locally bounded in time. item.description:

Modern machine learning relies on practical optimization methods that often differ from the algorithms studied in classical analyses: they train submodels, clip or normalize gradients, use layer-wise non-Euclidean directions, or approximate costly inner computations. By computing Newton corrections in lower-dimensional subspaces, the proposed methods aim to reduce computational costs while preserving the global $\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2}\right)$ convergence rate in function values of the full-space method. item.description:

This paper extends the least-squares and certainty-equivalence minimum-variance framework of classical linear self-tuning regulators to a broad class of nonlinearly parameterized systems with compact parameter spaces, including commonly used deep neural network models. With quadratic running costs, randomized exploration can change the optimal mean feedback.
